(a) Reduction in Term of Service.—Section 11–908A(c)(1), District of Columbia Official Code, is amended by striking “5 years” and inserting “3 years”. 
    (b) Effective Date.—The amendment made by subsection (a) shall apply with respect to any individual serving as a judge on the Family Court of the Superior Court of the District of Columbia on or after the date of the enactment of this Act.

fable.w: This section only shortens the required term of service for judges on the Family Court of the D.C. Superior Court and sets an effective date. There is no tempting reading here: it involves no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue for any party outside the federal government.
fable.s: Section 11–908A(c)(1), District of Columbia Official Code, is amended by striking “5 years” and inserting “3 years”.

qwen_block.w: This section amends the term of service for judges on the Family Court of the Superior Court of the District of Columbia. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or tribes) in the decision-making process. The change is a direct legislative amendment to a code section regarding judicial tenure.
qwen_block.s: Section 11–908A(c)(1), District of Columbia Official Code, is amended by striking “5 years” and inserting “3 years”.

opus.w: This section only amends the D.C. Code to cut the Family Court judges' term of service from 5 years to 3 and sets an effective date. Nothing in it is on the topic of participation: no consultation with outside parties, no hearing or comment period, no advisory body, no rulemaking and no right to sue. Mentioning judges and a court is not enough, because nothing here brings outside parties into a federal decision.
opus.b:
**Step 1: Analysis.** One might be tempted to read this as being about judges or courts and conclude it involves participation. But this section only shortens the required term of service for Family Court judges in D.C. Superior Court from 5 years to 3, and says when that change takes effect. No outside party is consulted, there is no hearing or comment period, no rulemaking is authorized, and no one is given a right to sue.

**Step 2: Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section amends the term of service for judges on the Family Court of the Superior Court of the District of Columbia. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or participation by parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or private entities) in a federal decision. The change is purely administrative regarding the tenure of judicial officers.
qwen_chat.s: (a) Reduction in Term of Service.—Section 11–908A(c)(1), District of Columbia Official Code, is amended by striking “5 years” and inserting “3 years”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing the term of service for judges affects the composition of the court and thus involves public participation. However, this is merely an administrative change to the tenure of federal (or D.C. quasi-federal) judicial officers. It does not create a mechanism for outsiders to consult with, advise, or participate in the decision-making process of the government. The actors involved are the judges themselves and the legislative body making the change, all of whom are inside the government structure.
